tests.stimulus: First use LUI/ADDI to write distinct nonzero values to all of x1 through x31 and execute several sequential instructions; assert rst_n on a falling edge and hold it across 3 rising edges, then use SW to read out all registers one by one after deassertion. Hold load and store instructions separately during reset and check that memory-access decoding is not gated by reset; the PC must not asynchronously clear to zero between edges, and the PC is 0 after a reset edge. Drive known inputs on falling edges and hold them across the execution rising edge; sample when combinational logic is stable before the edge, then wait 1ns after the rising edge for NBA and combinational propagation to complete before sampling again. Synchronous reset must be checked across rising edges; unknown state before the first reset is not compared.
tests.expected: One instruction executes on each rising edge of clk. A rising edge with rst_n at 0 clears the PC and all general-purpose registers to zero; reset is synchronous. During reset, the instruction-decoded dmem_re_o and dmem_we_o are still generated combinationally from the current instruction and are not gated by rst_n. External memory does not commit writes on reset edges. Reset deassertion and input updates occur on falling edges and remain stable across the next rising edge.

Drive known inputs on falling edges and hold them across the execution rising edge; sample when combinational logic is stable before the edge, then wait 1ns after the rising edge for NBA and combinational propagation to complete before sampling again. Synchronous reset must be checked across rising edges; unknown state before the first reset is not compared.
tests.expected: Neither the instruction interface nor the data interface has ready, stall, or response latency. imem_addr_o is the current 32-bit PC, and the environment provides a stable 32-bit instruction before the next execution rising edge; dmem_rdata_i is the read value of the aligned 32-bit word containing the current address. The model and DUT receive the same external input history. All arithmetic is modulo 32 bits. The legal input domain is known 0/1; exceptions, interrupts, and caches are not required.

Register values can be observed through subsequent store operations and instruction-address transfers; no internal access port is provided.
